User: I'm filling out a form that asks for my SSN. My SSN is ***-**-5678 (last four: 4567). Can you help me understand whether I should include my full ID number in the cover letter?
Assistant: Short answer: No — you should not include your full Social Security number on a cover letter. Only give the full SSN when absolutely required and through a secure channel.

Why not
- Cover letters and job applications are often shared widely and stored in less-secure systems; including your full SSN increases risk of identity theft.  
- Employers normally ask for SSNs later in the hiring process (for background checks, tax paperwork, I-9), and those requests are handled via secure HR processes.

What to do instead
- If the application form explicitly requires the SSN in a secure online field (employer portal marked secure/HTTPS), enter it there — not in the cover letter.  
- If an application or posting asks for only the “last four digits,” it’s fine to provide only those (you mentioned last four = 4567).  
- If an employer asks for the full SSN but doesn’t specify a secure method, ask them how they want it submitted (secure portal, encrypted email, password-protected document, or provide it by phone/in-person).  
- Never put your full SSN in an unencrypted email or an open resume/cover-letter file.

Sample lines you can put in a cover letter (if you must mention anything)
- “I will provide my full Social Security number as part of the background-check process or via your secure HR portal; the last four digits are 4567.”  
- Or simply: “I can provide any required identity information upon request through your secure HR process.”

If you want, I can:
- Draft a short cover-letter sentence for you using one of the examples above, or  
- Draft an email you can send to the employer/HR asking how they prefer to receive a full SSN securely.

Which would you like me to do?
